summary: Configured and verified a persistent, loopback-only SSH tunnel from node2:9082 to node1:9081. Recovery after connection interruption and sequential reboots of both nodes passed.
actions_performed: Added a boot-enabled OpenRC service for the unchanged supplied application on node1.
Created a dedicated restricted SSH identity permitting only local forwarding to 127.0.0.1:9081.
Added a supervised, boot-enabled tunnel service on node2 with keepalives and automatic respawn.
Verified listener isolation, document integrity, interruption recovery, and reboot persistence.
Preserved Alpine Linux v3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts.

evidence.requirement: Node1 application and node2 tunnel operate only on their respective loopback ports
evidence.summary: Shows healthy services, listeners on 127.0.0.1:9081 and 127.0.0.1:9082, and the expected status document through both endpoints.

evidence.requirement: Other cluster hosts have no direct application-listener access
evidence.summary: Direct requests to both node-address ports fail while loopback requests succeed.
Effective policy requires public-key authentication, permits only local forwarding to 127.0.0.1:9081, and disables sessions, TTY, agent, X11, and gateway binding.

evidence.requirement: Tunnel automatically recovers after a brief SSH interruption
evidence.summary: The live SSH process was terminated; a different PID appeared automatically and served the original response.

evidence.requirement: Supplied application and status document remain preserved
evidence.summary: Initial and final SHA-256 hashes match on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on Alpine Linux v3.23 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, boot ID change from 50047a1f… to 0413c899…, recovered app/data, and recovered downstream tunnel.
